findings.reason: the section must name the operator-run path (`--rehearse` from a plain shell on the fleet node, with the worker writing only the fragment) or the reckon change that grants a node the fleet state paths, or the node is undeliverable exactly as written.
findings.text: §5 tells the node to write `~/.config/zellij/layouts/probe-<name>.kdl` itself ("the node first writes a layout … with two tabs"), but `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1773` (`_require_write_paths_in_authority`) admits only resolved repository roots or `delivery_roots()` and offers no override, and the plan's own comment `c-s5-authority` (line 581) records that this exact command was refused at launch for writing `~/.config/zellij/layouts/` and `~/.local/state/fleet/migration/rehearsals/`; as written, a coordinator dispatching §5 hands the worker a step it is fenced out of, and the section's done-when ("that new rehearsal ledger, created after dispatch") would never be reached

findings.reason: the plan's only link to that gate's evidence is dead, so a reader cannot open the artifact the gate's `passed` verdict rests on, and the pointer must be reduced to the artifact path.
findings.text: the `r-gate-evidence` anchor for the passed gate `g-tfnsis-stop-path` has `href="the §2 fragment docs/evidence/fragments/…/name-how-a-stopped-worker-step-ends.html (commit 66610d127) names the srun client … reproduced 3 of 3"`, i.e. the human-readable Evidence sentence was written into the `href` attribute; resolving it as `<path>.html` cannot help because the value is prose with spaces, not a path

findings.reason: the frequency claim is the section's motivation, and a count of identity-moving commits on the first-parent history (the snapshot's own measurement should be taken over HEAD movement, not over repository commit count) changes how urgent the node is and what a reader believes about probe herd frequency.
findings.text: §11 argues the herd is frequent from "in the preceding 24 hours, 152 commits moved `reckon/`", but the identity a follower reads is fixed by what HEAD names, so commits on worker branches that never reach main's HEAD do not move it and do not start a herd; the figure overstates how often the condition this section fixes actually occurs

findings.reason: a measure whose only control is the base arm shows the change does work but not that its guard can fire, and the honest control is a tree whose recorded verdict is an import failure, which the asker must return rather than re-probe (the section's own bullet already needs this case named as the control).
findings.text: §11's done-when lists five tests and a measurement, and its only control is the base-revision positive control ("sixteen probes run"); no negative control is declared, so the node never shows that a recorded verdict can carry a failure, or that the one-proof guard can be made to produce the wrong answer it exists to prevent

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the evidence link on the passed gate `g-tfnsis-stop-path` carries a prose sentence in its `href` instead of a path, so the one pointer a reader has to that gate's evidence does not resolve (extensionless resolution as `<path>.html` does not rescue a string of prose).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §11's done-when names a positive control (the base-revision sixteen-probe arm) but declares no negative control, and the only falsifying arms it lists are guard tests, so nothing in the node shows the recorded-verdict path carrying a bad verdict.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the changed sections record into the plan's fragment directory (`docs/evidence/fragments/the-fleet-node-stays-in-service/`) and take measurements on the fleet allocation; no path names a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5, §10 and §11 name mechanisms (`source_code_identity`, `_committed_reload_tree`, `reckon_imports`, `ImportProbeTimedOut`, `IDENTITY_UNKNOWN`) and carry no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers into code or comments; the run ids and commit shas that appear are plan prose, which owns them.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5's stated mechanism (the node writes the probe layout itself, then asks the supervisor to start the session) cannot run on the real code path, because dispatch confines a node's write paths to repositories and delivery roots with no override and the layout lives under the operator's home; the plan's own comment `c-s5-authority` records exactly this refusal and §5 has not been reconciled with it. A second, smaller finding: §11's "152 commits moved `reckon/`" counts commits that never move the identity a follower reads at HEAD.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 (a rehearsal at the head), §10 (identity read only on HEAD movement) and §11 (one import proof per tree) each carry one deliverable and one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the driving followup `f-tfnsis-001` orders §10 before §11 and §5 after §4, and both declared gates (`g-tfnsis-stop-path` s2→s3, `g-tfnsis-move-ready` s5→s8) name sections that exist.
